why_included: Best current example of the "free internet access for agents" pitch with an unusually explicit install/doctor boundary.
verified_replacement_claim: PARTIAL: it can replace some paid scraping/search/API access, but not platform risk or maintenance.
cost_reality: Local install is cheap; operational cost appears later in cookies, proxies, breakage and platform drift.

why_included: Important benchmark for the "replace Devin" claim and for how far open coding agents have moved toward full environment control.
verified_replacement_claim: PARTIAL: it replaces part of the coding-agent workflow, not the entire product or reliability envelope.
cost_reality: Expect model/API spend plus real environment supervision.

why_included: Strong example of agent-tooling infrastructure that tries to replace dozens of bespoke integrations at once.
verified_replacement_claim: REAL for integration scaffolding, not for every hosted workflow layer above it.
cost_reality: Open source code does not remove auth, provider and maintenance complexity.

why_included: Good case study for observability software that sounds optional until prompts, costs and regressions pile up.
verified_replacement_claim: REAL against parts of LangSmith-style observability; the hosted convenience layer remains a separate question.
cost_reality: Storage, tracing volume and hosting still have a bill.

why_included: Owner project earns inclusion because it addresses agent workflow discipline rather than pretending to be another app.
verified_replacement_claim: SITUATIONAL: replaces ad-hoc prompt packs, private playbooks and some review checklists more than any single SaaS product.
cost_reality: Cheap to install, but only valuable if a team already works seriously with coding agents.

why_included: Owner project earns inclusion because repo instruction drift is real and the product has a clear bounded contract.
verified_replacement_claim: SITUATIONAL: replaces manual repo-agent contract maintenance, not a mainstream SaaS line item.
cost_reality: Low runtime cost; higher value only for repos that actually use agents in delivery.

why_included: The cleanest reminder that one open model can erase a very specific subscription category while leaving the rest intact.
verified_replacement_claim: PARTIAL: it replaces transcription, not meeting-product UX, collaboration or workflow.
cost_reality: Local compute is free only if you ignore the machine and time.

why_included: Useful because the source PDF is already stale here; the book should show how fast these categories rename and reposition themselves.
verified_replacement_claim: PARTIAL: self-hosted answer engines can substitute for some Perplexity-style queries, not the whole product experience.
cost_reality: Search quality and external model/search dependencies move the cost rather than remove it.

why_included: A broader local meeting stack than Whisper alone, useful for testing how much "meeting SaaS" can be decomposed.
verified_replacement_claim: PARTIAL: it can replace parts of Otter/Granola-style capture and summarization, not the full product promise.
cost_reality: Audio capture, transcription quality and local workflow rough edges remain your problem.

why_included: Worth keeping because "generate a presentation" is exactly the kind of promise that looks cheaper than it is.
verified_replacement_claim: PARTIAL: can replace some prompt-to-slide software, not editorial judgment or design taste.
cost_reality: Model/API cost and cleanup still exist.

why_included: Strong example of content automation ambition colliding with the cost of actually producing watchable media.
verified_replacement_claim: PARTIAL: replaces parts of AI video SaaS for teams willing to run the pipeline themselves.
cost_reality: API usage, rendering time, voice/media quality and workflow maintenance are the real bill.

why_included: Useful as a blunt utility reminder: sometimes the best open-source alternative is not a platform but a ruthlessly competent tool.
verified_replacement_claim: REAL for download utility use cases; not a replacement for whole media workflows.
cost_reality: Operationally cheap, but legally and policy-wise context matters.

why_included: The default serious candidate when someone says they want to stop paying Zapier.
verified_replacement_claim: REAL for a large class of automation tasks.
cost_reality: The invoice becomes server uptime, upgrades, debugging and process ownership.

why_included: Keeps the database-first Airtable alternative slot without bloating the book with near-duplicates.
verified_replacement_claim: PARTIAL to REAL depending on whether you already have SQL underneath.
cost_reality: The cheap part is the UI; the expensive part is still data design and responsibility.

why_included: Best current CRM case for testing how far open source really gets toward Salesforce-class ambition.
verified_replacement_claim: PARTIAL: clearly a real CRM, but "replaces Salesforce" is much too broad.
cost_reality: Self-hosting still means running a CRM platform with PostgreSQL, Redis and queues or paying for the cloud version.

why_included: Strong candidate because support inbox software is a tangible cost center and the value proposition is easy to understand.
verified_replacement_claim: REAL for many Intercom/Zendesk-style inbox needs.
cost_reality: Channels, storage, upgrades and team process still cost real effort.

why_included: Clear, bounded replacement story for owned mailing-list operations.
verified_replacement_claim: REAL for newsletter and list-management workflows.
cost_reality: The bill moves into email deliverability, hosting and list hygiene.

why_included: Too important to ignore, but useful only if the book stays skeptical about the everything-platform framing.
verified_replacement_claim: PARTIAL: real alternative to parts of Firebase; much weaker claim against specialized vector/database products.
cost_reality: You either pay Supabase or you operate a Postgres platform and its surrounding services yourself.

why_included: One of the clearest examples where open source can genuinely replace a bloated default.
verified_replacement_claim: REAL for many Google Analytics replacement needs.
cost_reality: Hosting and traffic cost exist, but the operational burden is still relatively sane.

why_included: Good example of software many people would love to self-host right up to the moment they discover backup responsibility.
verified_replacement_claim: REAL for a lot of Google Photos-style personal archive use.
cost_reality: Storage, backup, migration and trust in your own ops are the actual bill.

why_included: Useful scene-setting catalog, but not honest enough as a standalone replacement case.
verified_replacement_claim: MOSTLY MARKETING as a "replacement" entry; it is a directory, not a product.
cost_reality: The hidden cost is time spent assembling a stack from free tiers.

why_included: Good comparison point next to n8n, but not strong enough to deserve another full automation chapter page.
verified_replacement_claim: REAL for some Zapier/Make workflows, but overlaps heavily with n8n.
cost_reality: Similar operational burden to n8n without enough extra editorial yield for a full page here.

why_included: Useful map of the territory, not a product.
verified_replacement_claim: MOSTLY MARKETING if framed as a SaaS replacement; it is a catalog.
cost_reality: The cost is not money but choice overload and quality variance.

why_included: Good canonical reference for protocol readers who want to dig deeper after the main book.
verified_replacement_claim: NOT A REPLACEMENT PRODUCT.
cost_reality: The cost is implementation work, because protocol references do not deploy themselves.
